stemBlocks.value: Solve the simultaneous equations y = x − 2 and x² − xy = 8.
Think first: Substitute and watch what happens — the x squared terms may cancel, leaving something much simpler than expected.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p111-q08 from workbook page 111.

solutionSteps.instruction: Substitute y = x − 2 into the second equation.
Expand the product, distributing the minus sign across the bracket.
Simplify — the x squared terms cancel.
Solve for x, find y, and check.

strategyBlocks.value: Replace y with x − 2 in x² − xy = 8, expand carefully, and solve whatever equation remains.

whyThisWorks.value: The substitution removes the x squared term entirely, because x² − x(x − 2) simplifies to 2x, so the system is really linear in disguise. That is why there is only one solution instead of the usual two: the line y = x − 2 meets the curve x² − xy = 8 exactly once. The cancellation is genuine, not a lost solution.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Expanding −x(x − 2) as −x² − 2x and getting 4x = 8.

commonErrors.misconception: Assuming there must be two answers and inventing a second.

examTip.value: Distribute a negative sign across every term inside the bracket and write that line out in full — sign slips here change the whole answer.
